title: A Choppy Course to an Uncertain Future- Transportation Fuels Prospects 2009-2015
section_path: A Choppy Course to an Uncertain Future- Transportation Fuels Prospects 2009-2015
section_path_text: A Choppy Course to an Uncertain Future- Transportation Fuels Prospects 2009-2015
summary:
Transportation Fuels Prospects 2009‐2015,
The global economic crisis has slowed the forces that drove crude oil prices to record highs in the summer of 2008, but economists generally concede it has not stopped them. Coming years will force the energy industry to satiate developing world demand growth with an uncertain refining capacity footprint while under environmental constraints and persistent geopolitical risk. The period until 2015 will be most influential in forming a foundation from which the industry will face a future loaded with enormous challenges.

children.title: Desperately Seeking Demand
children.summary: In its most recent report, the IEA estimates that worldwide oil demand this year will fall to an average of 83.2 million barrels per day; a 3 percent drop from 2008. The global slowdown has had a chilling effect on the petroleum industry: Crude oil prices and product demand have both fallen and their decline has slowed some major refinery projects which could significantly impact the timing of future supply.

children.title: A Shifting Landscape
children.summary: Upon the eventual recovery of oil demand, participants will encounter a market where established supply roles are evolving quickly and new pricing relationships are being forged. The petroleum industry's center of activity has shifted eastward to the developing nations of Asia‐ led by China and India‐ where new refining capacity amid stagnant worldwide demand has chipped away at the "Asian premium" that previously added cost to barrels headed eastward.

children.title: Known Unknowns
children.summary: While supply and demand fundamentals along with price arbitrage will determine its basic direction, the international transportation fuels market will confront an increasingly complex environment in the years to come. In attempting to project that future environment, technology and policy are the biggest unknowns.

children.title: Asian Recovery Leads the Way
children.summary: The economic crisis will continue to dampen demand in the near‐term, but the fundamental assumption that links economic development with transportation sector growth remains essentially unchanged. Middle‐class aspiration was the driving force behind the expansion of the automobile in the United States and is not an exclusively American phenomenon.
